info.name: Task Tracker API
info.description:
API collection for the QA task tracker.

**Setup:** import `local.postman_environment.json`, select the *Task Tracker - local* environment and fill in `adminPassword`.

**Run order matters:** the folders build on each other (sign up -> log in -> create a task -> ...). Run the whole collection with the Collection Runner, or send requests top to bottom.

Tokens and ids are saved into collection variables by the test scripts, so you never copy them by hand. Each run creates its own user and cleans up after itself.

item.name: 1. Auth
item.description: Sign up and log in. Saves {{userToken}} and {{adminToken}}.

request.description: Creates a fresh regular user for this run. The pre-request script generates a unique username/password.

exec: // A unique user per run, so the collection can be run again and again.
pm.test("New accounts get the 'user' role", () => pm.expect(user.role).to.eql("user"));
pm.test("Password (or its hash) is never returned", () => pm.expect(user).to.not.have.any.keys("password", "password_hash"));

item.name: Sign up - username already taken (any case)

request.description: Usernames are unique regardless of upper/lower case.

exec: pm.test("Error message mentions \"Username must be\"", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.include("Username must be"));
pm.test("Error message mentions \"Invalid username or password\"", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.include("Invalid username or password"));

item.name: Log in as the new user

request.description: Saves the token as {{userToken}}; the Tasks and Comments folders use it.

exec: pm.test("Logged in as the right user", () => pm.expect(res.user.username).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("username")));

request.description: Uses adminUsername/adminPassword from the environment. Saves the token as {{adminToken}}.

exec: pm.test("Token belongs to the new user", () => pm.expect(me.username).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("username")));
pm.test("Has id, username, role, created_at", () => pm.expect(me).to.have.all.keys("id", "username", "role", "created_at"));

item.name: 2. Tasks
item.description: Task CRUD as a regular user.

exec: pm.test("New user is in the list", () => pm.expect(users.map(u => u.username)).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("username")));

request.description: PATCH only changes the fields you send.

exec: pm.test("Title untouched", () => pm.expect(task.title).to.eql("Login button does nothing"));
pm.test("History records the change", () => pm.expect(last.message).to.eql("Status changed from 'To Do' to 'In Progress'"));

pm.expect(task.description).to.eql("Only reproducible on Chrome. Firefox works.");
pm.test("One history entry per changed field", () => {

request.description: Sending the current value again must not add a history entry.

exec: pm.test("Oldest entry is the creation entry", () => pm.expect(history[0].message).to.match(/^Ticket created on /));
pm.test("All changes so far are listed", () => pm.expect(history.length).to.eql(Number(pm.collectionVariables.get("historyCount"))));

request.description: The author is taken from the token.

exec: pm.test("Error message mentions \"Comment is required\"", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.include("Comment is required"));
pm.test("Last entry is 'Comment added'", () => pm.expect(history[history.length - 1].message).to.eql("Comment added"));

item.name: 4. Validation & permissions
item.description: Requests that must fail, with the right status code.

request.description: Missing required fields are rejected by request validation.

exec: pm.test("Error message mentions \"Title is required\"", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.include("Title is required"));
pm.test("Error message mentions \"not a registered user\"", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.include("not a registered user"));

item.name: Delete task - as a regular user

exec: pm.test("Error message mentions \"Admin access required\"", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.include("Admin access required"));

5. Admin
item.description: Admin-only endpoints. Cleans up the task and user created by this run.

exec: pm.test("Counts every status", () => pm.expect(s.tasks_by_status).to.have.all.keys("To Do", "In Progress", "In Review", "Done"));
pm.test("Per-status counts add up to the total", () => pm.expect(Object.values(s.tasks_by_status).reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0)).to.eql(s.total_tasks));
pm.test("At least the admin and the new user exist", () => pm.expect(s.total_users).to.be.at.least(2));
